But he was also my father. And I know that for many of you, he was a man you loved, or a man you knew in a different way. I know there are memories here that are not mine.

I don’t know if I can fully reconcile those things. I don’t know if I can separate the man from the harm he caused. But I do know that I am here, and I am standing with the rest of you.

I want to honor the truth of what we survived. We survived him. We survived the drinking, the fear, and the years that were hard. And I think part of honoring him is acknowledging that we are still here, and that we are still whole, despite him.

I don’t know if he found peace before he died. I hope he did. I hope he found some rest from the things that drove him.

But today, I want to focus on us. On the family that remained. On the children who grew up and learned that they were worthy of love, even when he couldn’t give it.

I loved him, in my own way. And I grieve him, in my own way. And I am grateful for the peace that comes after the storm.

Thank you for being here."
